description:
Spotted while building the bd-95p test fixtures.

`bn init` in a repo whose `origin` is unreachable prints:

    ERROR error: failed to fetch from remote

...and then goes ahead and initialises the store anyway, exiting in a way that
reads as success. So the user sees a red ERROR line and a working store, and
cannot tell which of these happened:

  a) init failed and they must retry, or
  b) init succeeded locally and only the initial remote fetch failed (which is
     fine and expected offline).

It is (b). But nothing says so.

Offline / air-gapped init is a legitimate and supported thing — CLAUDE.md's
Offline First principle says so explicitly. So the fix is NOT to make this fail.
It is to stop calling a survivable condition an ERROR:

  * demote to a WARNING, and
  * say what it means and what to do: "store initialised locally; could not
    reach <remote> to fetch existing state. If the remote has an existing beads
    store, run `bn sync` once you are online before creating issues."

That last clause matters — initialising locally when the remote ALREADY has a
store is the one genuinely risky case (two divergent roots), and the current
message gives no hint of it.
title: kopi-beans: 'bn init' against an unreachable remote prints ERROR but still initialises and looks successful
